case.title: A new formulation after an existing NIR pilot
case.text: Our existing NIR pilot follows API concentration in one powder formulation at the tablet press feed frame. We are introducing a different API and excipient blend and would like to reuse the calibration. A colleague suggests adding Raman so that the old calibration will remain valid. What should our first technical assessment and experiment be?

refs.docTitle: Multispectral Laboratory of Optical Analysis Methods
refs.quote: As the powder blend passes the probe tip, the system captures spectra at high speeds without interrupting the production flow.
refs.claim: For powder blends (tablet press feed frame) NIR reflection and Raman probes measure the blend as it passes the probe tip.

refs.docTitle: Multispectral Laboratory of Optical Analysis Methods
refs.quote: NIR spectroscopy, with its relatively large penetration depth (up to several millimetres) even into dense solid samples due to low absorption and strong scattering
refs.claim: NIR penetrates several millimetres even into dense solids and powders because of low absorption and strong scattering.

related.docTitle: Multispectral Laboratory of Optical Analysis Methods
related.quote: strong absorption in the mid-IR region limits the corresponding spectral method to the analysis of very thin samples (usually less than 50 μm), but it opens up the possibility of using attenuated total reflectance (ATR)
related.claim: Mid-IR absorbs so strongly that only very thin layers (<50 µm) can be measured – in practice via ATR.

related.docTitle: Multispectral Laboratory of Optical Analysis Methods
related.quote: ATR fiber probes (Fig.1) enable the analysis of liquids and solid elastic samples, such as biological tissue, using specialized probes utilizing high-transmission fiber optics in the Mid-IR region.
related.claim: Mid-IR ATR fiber probes analyse liquids and elastic solids such as biological tissue.

related.docTitle: Multispectral Laboratory of Optical Analysis Methods
related.quote: A multispectral fiber probe, e.g. one combining MIR-ATR and fluorescence techniques into a single fiber optic probe shaft allows for the simultaneous acquisition of complementary chemical information from the exact same measurement point
related.claim: Heterogeneous solids like tissue need a combined probe that measures both methods at exactly the same point.

related.docTitle: Multispectral Laboratory of Optical Analysis Methods
related.quote: For highly transparent liquids with low optical density, UV-Transmission or Transflection probes are ideal
related.claim: Clear liquids with low optical density: transmission or transflection probes with a defined 1–10 mm path give high sensitivity for low concentrations.

related.docTitle: Multispectral Laboratory of Optical Analysis Methods
related.quote: as the media becomes more opaque, turbid, or highly concentrated, the signal in a standard transmission setup becomes saturated because the light cannot penetrate the bulk of the sample
related.claim: Opaque, turbid or highly concentrated media saturate a transmission setup because light cannot pass through the sample.

related.docTitle: Multispectral Laboratory of Optical Analysis Methods
related.quote: In these high-OD scenarios, a UV-ATR (Attenuated Total Reflection) probe is used.
related.claim: For high optical density liquids an ATR probe is used: the evanescent wave gives a path of a few micrometres, so black or highly scattering fluids can be measured without dilution.

related.docTitle: Multispectral Laboratory of Optical Analysis Methods
related.quote: Inline NIR Reflection is primarily used for opaque or highly concentrated dairy products, such as yogurt, butter, or whole milk concentrates.
related.claim: Opaque or highly concentrated dairy products (yogurt, butter, milk concentrates) are measured in-line with NIR diffuse reflection.

related.docTitle: Multispectral Laboratory of Optical Analysis Methods
related.quote: NIR Transmission is the preferred method for transparent or semi-transparent liquids, such as skim milk, whey, or permeate.
related.claim: For transparent or semi-transparent liquids (skim milk, whey, permeate) NIR transmission is the preferred method.

related.docTitle: Multispectral Laboratory of Optical Analysis Methods
related.quote: it fails when the milk becomes too "thick" or fat-rich, as the light cannot penetrate the sample
related.claim: Transmission fails once the product becomes thick or fat-rich; reflection works in highly scattering media but is less representative for clear liquids.

related.docTitle: Multispectral Laboratory of Optical Analysis Methods
related.quote: In some cases, a Transflection probe can already be a combined solution working well for low-fat and high-fat containing milk products.
related.claim: A transflection probe can sometimes cover both low-fat (clearer) and high-fat products with one interface.

related.docTitle: AFS Process Control Slides
related.quote: Spectra of API in hot polymer obtained with Diamond cone ATR probe coupled to iC10 FTIR (MTAC)
related.claim: API in hot polymer melt was measured with a diamond ATR probe.

related.claim: NIR light penetrates up to about 3 mm into tissue – deeper than other suitable spectral regions.

related.claim: Fiber probes are indispensable for local analysis of inhomogeneous solids (pharma and food products, soils, tissue).

related.quote: Although ATR spectroscopy is not optimal for the analysis of solid objects, its application for the analysis of biological tissues by fiber-based probes is one of the most important exceptions.
related.claim: ATR is not optimal for solid objects; biological tissue is an important exception.

related.docTitle: Combined MIR ATR and Fluorescence Fiber Probe (2021)

related.claim: Fluorescence light reaches a few millimetres into tissue, while ATR samples only a few micrometres.

recommendation.text: Worth testing because Raman scattering works on powders, offers high chemical selectivity and uses the same probe geometry as the existing NIR setup [E9, E10, E11].
Worth testing as diffuse‑reflection NIR is proven for powder blends and matches the current in‑line configuration [E12, E10].
Worth testing if a non‑contact geometry is preferred; it also handles powders effectively [E13, E10].
Worth testing in the laboratory to obtain high‑quality reference spectra before moving to an inline probe; not suitable for direct in‑line installation [E14, E15].

report.measurementConcept: An in‑process probe will be positioned at the tablet press feed frame to collect either Raman scattered light or diffuse‑reflection NIR from the moving powder stream; the probe is linked to a remote spectrometer via fibre optics, keeping the analyser away from vibration and dust [E1, E3, E5].
report.spectralRange: Raman probe operates in the visible to short‑wave NIR (≈400–1100 nm) with typical 785 nm excitation; NIR diffuse‑reflection probes cover 780–2500 nm. The exact usable range depends on the installed fibre type and length and must be verified for any mid‑IR option [E9, E12, E13].
risks: Matrix change makes the existing NIR calibration invalid (calibrations are matrix‑specific) [E8]
Uncertain fibre transmission may limit the spectral range or introduce losses
Optical variability (turbidity, bubbles) could degrade signal quality
Unknown API concentration range may require higher sensitivity than the tested methods provide
feasibilityPlan: 1. Install the Raman probe on the feed frame and connect it with the current fibre link; acquire Raman spectra of the new blend.
2. Use the existing NIR diffuse‑reflection probe (or surface‑at‑a‑distance probe) to collect NIR spectra under identical process conditions.
3. Collect independent reference concentrations (e.g., HPLC) for a set of samples covering the expected API range.
4. Build preliminary calibration models for Raman and NIR data and evaluate prediction errors against the reference values.
5. Compare the two techniques for signal quality, robustness to optical variability, and ability to meet the required detection change.
report.decisionBasis: A go decision will be made if a calibration model built from the new blend using Raman and/or NIR meets the client’s acceptable prediction error (as defined in the process monitoring specification). Failure to achieve the target error or inability to obtain reliable spectra due to fibre or optical variability will lead to a no‑go.

evidence.text: Immersible probes from UV to mid-IR measure liquids, soft and powdered solids in situ.
evidence.quote: Immersible fiber optic probes operating in various spectral regions from UV to mid-IR are increasingly being used for measuring liquid and soft or powdered solid samples.

evidence.text: Probe-based analysis is used in-line and in-process, and in situ for field tests or during surgery.
evidence.quote: Probe-based analysis is gaining widespread use in online analysis, such as in-line, in-process (chemical, biotechnological, natural) environments, as well as in-situ measurements, such as for field testing or for spectral diagnostics during surgery.

evidence.text: Fiber optics let the spectrometer stay away from vibration and dust while the probe sits in the process.
evidence.quote: The use of fiber optics is critical here, as it allows the sensitive spectrometers to be located safely away from the vibration and dust of the manufacturing floor.

evidence.text: Penetration depth differs between NIR, mid-IR and Raman, so each needs its own interface (ATR, transmission, transflection, reflection).
evidence.quote: Different absorption coefficients of light in NIR, Mid-IR, and Raman spectroscopy, as well as the depth of its penetration into a given dense medium (solid, liquid, or powder) also requires different measurement interfaces and techniques, such as various fiber optic probes: ATR, Transmission, Transflexion, Reflection, etc.

evidence.text: API content in powder blends: NIR and Raman give complementary chemical information.
evidence.quote: The combination of these techniques is particularly effective because it captures complementary chemical information: NIR detects hydrogen bonds and asymmetric polar groups, while Raman provides information on the molecular backbone and symmetrical non-polar groups.

evidence.text: Calibrations are matrix-specific. A changed formulation needs a new or extended calibration; adding another method does not keep the old model valid.
